one_line_delta: LSTMs stopped rewriting memory every step and started editing it.
hooks: An RNN's memory fades like a photocopy of a photocopy. LSTMs fixed it by not copying.
One number, set to 1, closed the gap between two famous AI architectures.

surprising_numbers.meaning: gradient left after 50 steps: vanilla RNN vs LSTM that learned to hold
an LSTM with forget bias 0 forgets faster than the RNN at the start of training
and no LSTM variant beat the standard one
time lags the 1997 LSTM could bridge

misconceptions.belief: LSTMs solve both vanishing and exploding gradients.
misconceptions.correction: They fix vanishing on the cell path; exploding gradients still need clipping.

misconceptions.belief: LSTMs always remember longer than RNNs.
misconceptions.correction: With forget bias 0 they start out forgetting faster; the gain comes from a path the optimiser can push toward 1.
The forget gate does most of the work; the output gate mattered little in ablations.

misconceptions.belief: The forget gate was part of the original LSTM.
misconceptions.correction: It was added three years later, in 2000.

visuals: photocopier re-copying a page vs a page on a conveyor belt being edited with sticky notes
gradient bar shrinking over 50 steps for each row of the decay table
three valves on a pipe labelled forget, input, output
analogy: If a vanilla RNN is a photocopier re-copying the whole page every step, an LSTM is a page on a conveyor belt edited with sticky notes: it swaps a full rewrite through a matrix and squash for additive edits controlled by learned valves.
